items.title: Australia Bonds Set for Longest Rally Since June on RBA Cut Bets
items.description: Australia’s bond market is heading for its longest rally in over five months as mounting signs of economic weakness fuel bets the Reserve Bank’s next move will be an interest-rate cut.

items.title: GQG Shares Set for Record Surge in Sydney With AI Trade Revival

items.title: Shares in Chinese Cobalt Producers Jump After Congo Bans Exports
items.description: Shares in Chinese cobalt producers surged after the Democratic Republic of Congo slapped an export ban on the battery metal from the end of the month in a bid to arrest a price decline.

items.description: Copper resumed a decline after a spike driven by Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia Corp., with investors still cautious about demand.

items.title: Copper Smelters Face Worsening Squeeze as Negotiations Stall
items.description: Copper smelters are bracing for a period of extreme financial pressure as closely-watched negotiations over supply contracts for next year go down to the wire.

items.title: Keppel Agrees to Merge Telecom Firms M1 and Starhub
items.description: Asset manager Keppel Ltd. agreed to combine M1 Ltd. with Starhub Ltd. in an all-share deal, bringing together two of Singapore’s major telecommunications operators following months of talks.

items.title: US Senate Probes Vance Role in Vitol Choice for Venezuela Oil
items.description: A US senator is investigating the role Vice President JD Vance played in awarding a lucrative Venezuelan oil contract to a political donor and then-executive at commodities trader Vitol Group.

items.title: Petrobras Makes $470 Million Ethanol Bet in Brazil With Neomille Stake
items.description: Brazil’s state-controlled oil producer Petrobras is buying a stake in corn-ethanol producer Neomille SA as part of a wider expansion into biofuels.

items.description: A White House pressure campaign and a $5 trillion market slide forced Nvidia to reinstate its founder — proving that in the AI race, boardroom discipline is a luxury shareholders can’t afford.
